subject: Post-call: Reserved capacity, isolation needs & risk assessment for CerebraTek
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reeves <alex@cerebratek.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@cerebratek.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Reserved capacity, isolation needs & risk assessment for CerebraTek

Alex / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we don’t lose momentum. I captured the highlights from our discussion and the asks we'll need to move towards a committed reserved capacity (dedicated GPUs + isolation). Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared
- Peak serving latency spikes during batch scoring windows (p99 > 500ms) causing timeouts in downstream pipelines.
- Cost unpredictability on current cloud bursts — need predictable unit economics for forecasting.
- Regulatory requirement to segregate PHI inference workloads into an isolated environment with customer-managed keys.

Goals (30–90 day horizon)
1) Stabilize online inference p99 latency to <200ms for standard prompts at production load.
2) Move 3 mission-critical models to a dedicated, isolated pool (red-team/PHI) with KMS/HSM support and audit logs.
3) Agree on a monthly committed GPU seat count and SLA (availability + latency SLOs) to support procurement.

Sizing & topology we discussed
- Initial committed footprint: 6 x A100 80GB-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool). We estimate this will support ~250 qps for short-context requests and ~100 qps for longer sequences with batching. See attached sizing spreadsheet for the working estimate.
- Isolation: dedicated pool (single-tenant) with separate networking/VPC and customer KMS integration.
- Autoscale/burst: reserved baseline of 6 GPUs with a 2x burst allowance for traffic spikes (pay-per-burst).
- Fallback: model-variant routing to lower-cost quantized profile if capacity constrained.

SLA targets discussed
- Uptime SLA: 99.9% monthly for reserved pool.
- Latency SLO: p99 < 200ms for standard prompt profile; p95 < 120ms.
- Incident response: 1-hour P1 acknowledgement + 4-hour mitigation window (we can formalize these in contract language).

Risks / open items you asked us to validate
- Confirm whether the dedicated pool can satisfy your SOC2/HIPAA evidence requests (we can provide our audit artifacts + a customer isolation playbook).
- Clarify procurement timeline and required contract terms (term length, termination, data residency).
- Validation run: you requested a 2-week pilot on a trial pool to validate latency under your realistic load.

Proposed next steps (owners & dates)
1) Hannah: Share sizing spreadsheet + SLAs (attached) — today (sent).
2) Ben: Follow-up with technical runbook and on-call coverage for pilot — by Tue, 2027-04-06.
3) Priyom: Loop in Ops & Security for KMS/HSM and SOC2 evidence; share questionnaire answers — by Thu, 2027-04-08.
4) Alex / Procurement: confirm procurement window and PO cadence; return any redlines — by Mon, 2027-04-12.

Attachments included: cerebratek_sla_request.pdf (requested SLA template), inference-sizing-estimate.xlsx (working capacity numbers).

If that looks right, I’ll schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff for Tue 2027-04-06 — suggested attendees: Ben (ops lead), Priyom (solutions eng), Alex (CTO) + one of your infra engineers.

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt

Thanks Hannah — this is great and exhaustive. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Sizing: the 6 x A100 estimate looks reasonable as a starting point. One ask: can you also include an alternate configuration using 4 x H100s (we’re evaluating availability vs cost)?
- Isolation: we must ensure keys are customer-managed and that audit logs are exportable to our SIEM (Splunk). We’ll send the SOC2/HIPAA questionnaire tomorrow.
- Pilot: confirmed — we can carve out a small window next week for a 10k-request/day smoke test (non-PHI), and then a second pilot with PHI in a scrubbed environment. What does Redwood need from us to run the first pilot?

Procurement note (from Procurement Team): we typically require 45–60 day lead time for contract review. Please include standard MSA + SOW in the packet.

Alex Reeves

Alex — quick tech note on the H100 vs A100 ask:
- H100s provide a better throughput/latency profile for transformer decoder workloads with longer context, but availability varies regionally. For predictable SLOs I recommend we model both (A100 baseline, H100 alternate) and include a recommended fallbacks sheet in the sizing workbook.

For the pilot we typically need:
- A short list of representative prompts + expected QPS profile.
- A non-PHI dataset for the smoke run (you can provide synthetic or scrubbed samples).
- A technical contact and one infra host we can test connectivity with (SSH/VPN/VPC peering details as applicable).

I’ll build a one-page pilot checklist and drop it into the shared MAP doc by EOD.

—Ben
